title: Light sources sort cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 15 (Light sources sort cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 15: Light sources: why do cat's eyes glow?. To understand that we need light to see and that some things give out light while others only reflect it

blocks.title: Sort into: Light source / Not a light source
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Light source, Not a light source.
blocks.answer: Light source: the Sun; a torch; a lamp; a candle flame. Not a light source: a mirror; the Moon; cat's eyes; road reflector

questions.q: Is the Moon a light source?
questions.a: No. It reflects light from the Sun.
questions.model: Ask: does it make its own light? The Moon does not. It shines because the Sun's light bounces off it. So it is not a light source.

questions.q: Put in order: light enters eye, light leaves Sun, light hits book.
questions.a: Light leaves Sun, light hits book, light enters eye.

questions.q: Core: Go around your home (with an adult). List 4 light sources and 4 things that only reflect light.
questions.a: Light sources: lamp, screen, torch, oven light. Reflect only: mirror, spoon, foil, window.
questions.model: Teacher does two first: a lamp (light source: it gives out light), a spoon (reflects: it only shines when light hits it).

questions.q: Extend: Draw arrows to show how you see a book in a room lit by a lamp.
questions.a: Arrow from lamp to book; arrow from book to eye.

questions.q: Stretch: Why can't you see anything in a sealed dark cupboard?
questions.a: No light can get in, so no light reflects into your eyes.

questions.q: Big question: do cat's eyes really make their own light?
questions.a: No. They reflect light that shines into them.
